title: T3 timeout - upstream communication lost
shortDescription: Modem sent a ranging request upstream but got no response from the CMTS before the T3 timer expired.
fullDescription:
A T3 timeout occurs when your Arris Surfboard modem transmits a ranging request to the cable modem termination system (CMTS) at your ISP, but no reply arrives within the allotted window. This usually points to upstream signal problems - too much noise, weak signal level, or line damage between the modem and the neighborhood node.

You will typically see T3 timeouts logged repeatedly in the modem's event log before the modem loses sync entirely. Internet drops intermittently then stops working completely.

Most T3 timeouts are caused by loose coax fittings, damaged splitters, degraded drop cables, or ISP-side plant issues. A reboot sometimes helps briefly but the underlying signal problem must be fixed.

causes.cause: Damaged drop cable from pole to house
ISP plant issue or node congestion
Ingress noise from faulty home wiring

fixSteps.title: Tighten all coax connections
fixSteps.instruction: Hand-tighten then use a wrench 1/8 turn more on every coax connector from wall to modem.

fixSteps.title: Remove unnecessary splitters
fixSteps.instruction: Connect modem directly to the wall outlet bypassing any splitters for testing.

fixSteps.title: Check signal levels in modem UI
fixSteps.instruction: Log in to 192.168.100.1 and review upstream power (should be 35-51 dBmV) and SNR (35+ dB).

fixSteps.title: Contact ISP
fixSteps.instruction: If levels are out of spec, schedule a technician visit to inspect the drop line.

whenToCallPro: If signal levels are out of spec after tightening connections, call your ISP for a line technician.

faq.q: Will replacing the modem fix T3 errors?
faq.a: Rarely. T3 errors point to line/signal problems, not the modem itself.
Between 35 and 51 dBmV for DOCSIS 3.0/3.1.

title: T1 timeout - no sync message received
shortDescription: Modem failed to receive a sync message from the CMTS within 600 ms.
fullDescription:
T1 timeouts happen on the downstream path - the modem is listening for periodic SYNC messages from the CMTS and has not received one. This indicates the modem either cannot lock a downstream channel or the signal is too weak/noisy to decode.

T1 errors usually appear alongside 'No Ranging Response received' and downstream scan loops. The modem will cycle through startup repeatedly and never complete registration.

Most commonly caused by very low downstream power, cable disconnected upstream of the modem, or CMTS-side outage.

causes.cause: Loose coax at wall or modem

fixSteps.title: Check ISP outage map
fixSteps.instruction: Visit your ISP's outage page or call the outage hotline before anything else.

fixSteps.title: Reseat coax at wall and modem
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and firmly reattach the coax cable on both ends.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle modem
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 30 seconds, plug back in, wait 3 minutes for full boot.

fixSteps.title: Try a known-good coax cable
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a different RG6 coax to rule out cable damage.

whenToCallPro: If ISP confirms no outage and downstream power is still out of spec, request a tech visit.
videoSearchQuery: Arris modem T1 timeout downstream fix

faq.a: Between -15 and +15 dBmV, ideally near 0 dBmV.

title: Online/Internet LED is off
shortDescription: Modem is powered and has signal but cannot complete registration with the ISP.
fullDescription:
When the Internet/Online LED stays dark while Power, Downstream and Upstream are solid, the modem has signal sync but is failing the final DHCP/registration handshake with the ISP. This usually means the modem is not provisioned on the account or the MAC address has not been registered.

Common after buying a used modem, moving, or when an ISP swaps provisioning systems.

fixSteps.title: Self-activate online
fixSteps.instruction: Visit your ISP's activation URL (e.g., xfinity.com/activate) from a phone on cellular data.

fixSteps.title: Call ISP with MAC address
fixSteps.instruction: Provide the modem's MAC (on the sticker) and ask to register it on your account.

fixSteps.title: Reboot after provisioning
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modem for 60 seconds after ISP confirms provisioning is complete.

whenToCallPro: Always start with the ISP - this is an account/provisioning issue.
videoSearchQuery: Arris modem online light not on activate

faq.q: Can I use any Arris modem?
faq.a: Only modems on your ISP's approved list will activate.

title: Modem stuck scanning downstream channels
shortDescription: Downstream LED flashes continuously as modem searches for a lockable carrier.
fullDescription:
The modem is in an endless downstream acquisition loop - it cannot find and lock onto a usable DOCSIS channel. The DS light blinks steadily rather than going solid. Often the modem eventually gives up and reboots.

Caused by absent or extremely weak downstream signal. If other services on the same coax (TV) also fail, the problem is upstream of the home.

fixSteps.title: Bypass splitters
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all splitters and connect modem directly to the wall.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coax connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check that center conductors are straight, clean and protrude ~1/8 inch.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset modem
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the reset button for 30 seconds with modem powered on.

fixSteps.title: Schedule ISP tech
fixSteps.instruction: If no signal is present at the wall, the drop or tap needs ISP attention.

whenToCallPro: When no signal is present even with modem plugged directly into the wall.
videoSearchQuery: Arris modem downstream scan loop fix

faq.q: How long should the DS light take to go solid?
faq.a: Typically under 60 seconds after power-on.

title: DHCP request to ISP timed out
shortDescription: Modem registered but failed to get an IP address lease from the ISP DHCP server.
fullDescription:
After ranging completes, the modem sends a DHCP DISCOVER to obtain a WAN IP. If the ISP's DHCP server does not reply, the modem logs 'Started Unicast Maintenance Ranging - No Response received - T3 time-out' or 'DHCP Timeout'. This is typically account/provisioning related.

Sometimes also caused by stale DHCP leases that a modem reboot clears.

causes.cause: Stale DHCP lease on ISP side

fixSteps.title: 30-second power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modem for 30+ seconds to release lease.

fixSteps.title: Confirm provisioning
fixSteps.instruction: Call ISP to verify the modem MAC is active on your account.

whenToCallPro: After a clean reboot if DHCP still times out, ISP support needs to flush the lease.

faq.q: Does this mean my router is bad?
faq.a: No - DHCP timeout on the modem refers to WAN-side DHCP from the ISP, not your LAN.

title: IPv6 provisioning failed
shortDescription: Modem obtained IPv4 but failed to acquire an IPv6 address/prefix.
fullDescription:
The modem logs DHCPv6 solicitation or RA failures. IPv4 works but IPv6 connectivity is missing. Some ISPs roll out IPv6 gradually so this may occur after a region-wide upgrade.

Often a firmware-side issue on older Arris models (SB6183 known to have IPv6 quirks) or an ISP provisioning problem.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle modem and router
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug both for 60 seconds, boot modem first then router.

fixSteps.title: Ask ISP to push firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Retail modems get firmware only from the ISP - request the latest push.

whenToCallPro: Persistent IPv6 failure after firmware push - consider replacing with DOCSIS 3.1 model.

faq.a: Yes for some streaming services and future-proofing, but IPv4 alone still works for most sites.

title: T2 timeout - no broadcast maintenance opportunity
shortDescription: Modem did not receive a broadcast maintenance opportunity during initial ranging.
fullDescription: T2 is the timer for receiving a broadcast maintenance opportunity from the CMTS during initial ranging. A T2 timeout means the modem saw the downstream but never got scheduled to transmit upstream. Often indicates a completely severed upstream path or a plant outage.

fixSteps.title: Check ISP outage map
fixSteps.instruction: Verify there is no known outage before troubleshooting.

fixSteps.title: Replace coax to modem
fixSteps.instruction: Try a different known-good RG6 cable.

whenToCallPro: Persistent T2 after cable swap - ISP line work needed.

faq.a: T2 usually means a harder signal loss than intermittent T3 errors.

title: CMTS did not respond to ranging request
shortDescription: Modem sent RNG-REQ but received no RNG-RSP from the CMTS.
fullDescription: During ranging, the modem repeatedly sends RNG-REQ messages. If the CMTS never responds with RNG-RSP, the modem logs 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out'. Often appears in bursts alongside T3 timeouts and indicates upstream signal instability.

fixSteps.title: Inspect home coax
fixSteps.instruction: Replace any old splitters with 5-1002 MHz rated units.

fixSteps.title: Request signal check from ISP
fixSteps.instruction: Have a tech measure upstream power at the tap.

whenToCallPro: Recurring ranging failures usually require a line tech.

faq.a: Yes - wet connectors and water ingress are a common trigger.

title: Upstream dynamic range window violation
shortDescription: Upstream channels are operating at different power levels outside the CMTS-allowed window.
fullDescription:
On DOCSIS 3.0/3.1 channel-bonded upstreams, the CMTS requires all channels to stay within a few dB of each other (the dynamic range window). If home wiring introduces tilt or one channel becomes attenuated, the modem logs DRW violations and may drop channels.

Commonly caused by old frequency-limited splitters or long cable runs.
symptoms: Channel bonding drops to fewer channels

fixSteps.title: Replace older splitters
fixSteps.instruction: Install 5-1002 MHz or 5-1218 MHz splitters throughout the home.

whenToCallPro: If new splitters do not resolve the tilt, call ISP for in-line amp evaluation.

faq.q: What splitter rating should I buy?
faq.a: At minimum 5-1002 MHz; prefer 5-1218 MHz for DOCSIS 3.1.

title: Modem firmware corrupted or boot looping
shortDescription: Modem reboots every few minutes and never completes registration.
fullDescription:
A rare but serious fault where firmware on the modem's flash becomes corrupted - usually after a failed ISP firmware push or a lightning event. The modem will cycle LEDs in a repeating pattern and never come online.

Retail DOCSIS modems cannot have firmware manually reflashed by end users; recovery requires the ISP to push a fresh image or RMA of the unit.

causes.cause: Flash wear after years of use

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset button 30 seconds - sometimes clears a corrupt config.

fixSteps.title: Ask ISP to push firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Support can trigger an over-the-air firmware push to a known-good image.

fixSteps.title: RMA or replace
fixSteps.instruction: If within warranty, contact Arris support for replacement.

whenToCallPro: If factory reset does not help, ISP or Arris RMA is the only route.

faq.a: No - retail cable modems do not expose user-accessible firmware flashing.
